title: vectorized-pacing-sandbox-notes-isa
content:
Notes to self - vectorized pacing sandbox

Goal:
- Explore a "vectorized" pacing approach where we bundle small concurrent inference requests into a single accelerated pipeline stage instead of traditional batching; keep tail latency bounded while increasing amortized GPU utilization.

Hypothesis:
1) For many short requests (<=128 tokens) with high qps, vectorized pacing reduces kernel launch overhead and KV cache thrash, improving p50/p95 without degrading p99 significantly.
2) Works best when sequence length distribution is narrow and model supports fused attention kernels.

Environment:
- small GPU pool: 4 x A100 40GB (dev cluster)
- runtime branch: feature/vectorized-pacing (see PR above)
- workload generator: ./tools/loadgen --profile=zipf-small --qps=1200 --concurrency=300
- model: llama2-13b-8bit-quant (ctx 2048), kv-cache enabled

Experiment matrix:
A) baseline: continuous-batching (timeout=5ms, max_batch=64)
B) vectorized-pacing: pack-window=8 (pack up to 8 concurrent requests into vector op), prefill-coalesce=true
C) vectorized-pacing + small cache-window=64 (avoid full cache eviction)

Commands run:
- baseline: ./bench/run.sh --mode=baseline --qps=1200 --duration=10m > baseline.log
- vect: ./bench/run.sh --mode=vector --pack=8 --qps=1200 --duration=10m > vect8.log
- vect+cache: ./bench/run.sh --mode=vector --pack=8 --cache=64 --qps=1200 --duration=10m > vect8-cache64.log

Quick raw observations (from parsed logs):
- baseline: p50=18ms, p95=54ms, p99=212ms, throughput achieved=1.02k qps (some drop from requested 1.2k), GPU util ~56%
- vect (pack=8): p50=14ms, p95=39ms, p99=265ms, throughput=1.18k qps, GPU util ~72%
- vect+cache64: p50=15ms, p95=37ms, p99=138ms, throughput=1.19k qps, GPU util ~71%

Interpretation:
- Packing (vectorized) reduces median and p95 by removing per-request overhead & better kernel packing.
- However naive packing increased p99 (265ms) — likely due to cache churn / longer coalesced prefill for stragglers.
- Adding small cache-window (cache=64) dramatically improved p99 to 138ms — suggests cache-residency is critical for tail behavior with packing.

Telemetry clues:
- Traces show straggler paths: a few requests hit cold KV loads during pack -> prefill became dominant for that pack and delayed whole vector op.
- Scheduling logs: pack waiting thresholds occasionally exceed 12ms during burst peaks. Need tighter backpressure/gating.

Charts I sketched (generate next):
- CDF overlay: baseline vs vect vs vect+cache (0-500ms) showing vect p99 spike and cache mitigation.
- GPU kernel timeline: fewer small kernels, longer fused kernels under vect.

Open questions / TODO:
- Tune pack timeout gate: current pack waits up to 8ms for partners; try 3ms and 12ms to see tail tradeoffs.
- Explore adaptive pack size (grow/shrink based on recent p99 history).
- Add per-request hazard: if a request flagged "sensitive" (high SLA), bypass packing and take dedicated fast-path.
- Instrument KV admission: when a pack contains >1 cold KV fill, maybe fall back to non-coalesced prefill to avoid amplifying stragglers.
- Run with heterogeneous sizes (mix short+long). Does vectorized pacing hurt long-latency requests?

Quick next steps (practical):
- Add experiment with pack_timeout=3ms and 12ms (two runs) and compare p99s.
- Add metric: percent_packs_with_any_cold_kv (add lightweight counter).
- Write small runbook for ops: if p99 > 200ms, disable packing via runtime flag.

Notes to self (less formal):
- This looks promising for PLG tier workloads where median/p95 matter most, but need guardrails for p99-sensitive customers.
- Keep an eye on memory pressure when we increase cache-window; 64 seemed OK in dev but try 32/128 as well.
- Talk to Marta about whether variant-fallback can be triggered at pack-level (i.e., if pack has >1 fragile request, route to warm-pool).

End of scratchpad. Save logs in /tmp/bench-results/vectorized-2024-11-15/ and upload summary to PR description.
